summary: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships a Go binary that remote-controls a local coding agent over WebRTC
details: The tarball's sole payload is a ~12MB Go executable at bin/sxt that links a full WebRTC/ICE/STUN/TURN/SCTP DataChannel stack (github.com/pion/webrtc/v4, github.com/pion/turn/v5) together with a QR-code library and Codex/Claude coding-agent orchestration logic. Binary symbols including executor.codexAppStream, executor.codexUsage, window.codexRoot, window.codexCand, window.approvalDecision, client.connectionAttempt, and ice.controllingSelector show the binary establishes a peer-to-peer data channel to a remote party and forwards command execution and approval decisions from that peer into a locally driven Codex/Claude agent on the installer's host. package.json declares its license as 'SEE LICENSE IN https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control' — the repo name and author handle match the binary's remote-control behavior and do not correspond to a recognizable vendor product named 'Sextant'. Once the shipped binary is launched, a remote peer that completes the WebRTC handshake (QR-code pairing) gains the ability to drive a coding agent with approval/exec authority on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
